_comment: Issue #1405: an infantry block that survives a cavalry charge (per-soldier melee, no formula wipe, no rout) used to never re-spread to its commanded pitch afterward -- a knocked-back soldier catching up to the block while it MARCHES (pursuing the withdrawing cavalry) would flip between a direct approach and a full flank-and-rear corridor detour every time its distance to its own slot hovered at the direct-arrival radius, flinging it a formation's-width away right as it was about to land. A 12-horse cycle-charge cavalry (armed via the J stance, same UI gesture as any other order) hits a 40-man, morale-2.2 infantry line hard enough to knock its front rank around without wiping or routing it, then peels back to recharge -- the infantry, still tracking its live target_enemy, keeps marching after it, which is exactly the condition that used to strand the knocked-back rank. The clip's subject is the re-spread itself: watch the infantry's front rank close back up to full spacing as the block marches, rather than trailing a loose straggling clump for the rest of the clip. The post-strike reform window itself (roughly t400-800) is deliberately NOT sampled -- while the knocked-back rank is still catching up to the marching block, nearest-neighbour distance legitimately dips below the overlap floor for individual samples even with the fix (real, bounded-acceleration recovery just takes a few seconds, it is not instantaneous); the sampled ticks pin the charge, the strike, and the SETTLED outcome once re-spread completes.
